Contributing to exposomeSC

Source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

Bug reports and pull requests are welcome at https://github.com/CuiweiG/exposomeSC/issues. Please open pull requests against main.

The rest of this page records how changes move between GitHub and Bioconductor. The two sides use different names for the development branch, which is the easiest place to make a mistake.

Which branch a change goes to

exposomeSC is in Bioconductor devel (3.25) and has no release branch yet.

Change GitHub branch Bioconductor branch Version
Any change before the Bioconductor 3.25 release main devel 0.99.z
After the 3.25 release: new features, changed defaults, refactoring main devel 1.1.z (odd y)
After the 3.25 release: bug fixes and documentation corrections RELEASE_3_25, after main RELEASE_3_25, after devel 1.0.z (even y)
  • GitHub main has the same code as Bioconductor devel but only our own commits; see Pushing.
  • The review is over: changes no longer go through BiocStaging/exposomeSC or the bioc-revision-2026-11 branch, but straight to Bioconductor’s own repository.
  • Once RELEASE_3_25 exists, a bug fix goes into main first and is then cherry-picked to RELEASE_3_25. Each branch gets its own version bump.

Version numbers

Bioconductor uses x.y.z version numbers (https://contributions.bioconductor.org/versionnum.html):

  • Until the 3.25 release the version stays at 0.99.z. At the release the Bioconductor team sets the release branch to 1.0.0 and devel to 1.1.0; after that, y is even on the release branch and odd on devel. Make the same change on main in a commit of our own, and do not change x or y otherwise.
  • Bump z in every commit that should reach users (0.99.4 to 0.99.5). A pushed commit without a version bump is built, but not propagated: BiocManager::install() keeps serving the previous version.
  • Commits that only touch files left out of the package by .Rbuildignore (for example .github/) do not need a bump.
  • Builds run once a day and take about 24 hours, so a push appears on the build report (https://bioconductor.org/checkResults/) one or two days later. It reaches users once a build with the new version finishes without errors.

Remotes

This is the setup Bioconductor recommends (https://contributions.bioconductor.org/git-version-control.html):

git remote add upstream git@git.bioconductor.org:packages/exposomeSC.git
git remote -v
# origin    https://github.com/CuiweiG/exposomeSC.git (fetch)
# origin    https://github.com/CuiweiG/exposomeSC.git (push)
# upstream  git@git.bioconductor.org:packages/exposomeSC.git (fetch)
# upstream  git@git.bioconductor.org:packages/exposomeSC.git (push)

ssh -T git@git.bioconductor.org info lists what the registered SSH key may read (R) and write (W); packages/exposomeSC should show R W.

Pushing

main keeps only our own commits. While devel has nothing else, the same commit goes to both sides:

git push upstream <hash>:refs/heads/devel
git push origin <hash>:refs/heads/main

Once the Bioconductor team has committed to devel (the version bumps at each release), never merge upstream/devel into main. Commit on main, then cherry-pick to devel:

git fetch upstream
git checkout -B bioc-devel upstream/devel
git cherry-pick <commits from main>
git push upstream <hash on bioc-devel>:refs/heads/devel
git push origin <hash on main>:refs/heads/main

Never force-push: Bioconductor does not accept rewritten history.

Continuous integration

The workflows in .github/workflows/ run on main with R-devel, which Bioconductor devel uses: R CMD check on Linux, macOS and Windows, BiocCheckGitClone() and BiocCheck(), test coverage, and a check of citation(), links and spelling. The pkgdown site is built from main. The versions are set at the top of each workflow; check them when Bioconductor 3.25 is released and RELEASE_3_25 appears.
